title: A universally exact sequence with finitely presented quotient splits
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A,B,C$ be $R$-modules, and let $i:A\to B$ and $p:B\to C$ be $R$-linear maps with $i$ injective, $p$ surjective and $\ker p=i(A)$. Suppose $C$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Suppose also that for every $R$-module $Q$ the sequence $0\to A\otimes_RQ\xrightarrow{i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q}B\otimes_RQ\xrightarrow{p\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q}C\otimes_RQ\to0$ is exact, meaning that its first map is injective, its last map is surjective and the image of its first map is the kernel of its last map [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then there exists an $R$-linear map $r:B\to A$ satisfying $r\circ i=\mathrm{id}_A$. No finite-generation or flatness assumption on $A$ or $B$ is made.

source.place: Tag 058L, label lemma-universally-exact-split, the universally exact implies split direction; the retraction form of splitting.

proof.text: The assumed tensor sequence is exact for every R-module Q, hence in particular its first map is injective for every finitely presented Q. After the canonical symmetry isomorphisms for tensor products over the commutative ring R, this is precisely the finitely-presented test condition in [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test] for the map i:A→B. Thus i⊗id_Q is injective for every finitely presented Q, and the full tensor sequence remains exact by the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 058K, theorem-universally-exact-criteria, (1) implies (2), restriction to finitely presented tensor tests.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation R^n --g₁--> R^m --g₂--> C -> 0, with g₂ surjective and g₂g₁=0. Lift g₂ through p to h₂:R^m -> B. Since p(h₂g₁)=g₂g₁=0 and ker p=i(A), there is h₁:R^n -> A with i h₁=h₂g₁. Write g₁(e_i)=∑_j a_{ij}d_j for bases (e_i) of R^n and (d_j) of R^m, and form the correctly oriented relation map t:R^m -> R^n by t(d_j)=∑_i a_{ij}e_i. Let Q=coker(t), which is finitely presented. The vector x=(h₁(e_i))_i∈A^n maps under i^n to (h₂g₁(e_i))_i=(∑_j a_{ij}h₂(d_j))_i, hence its class in B⊗_R Q is zero because the image of B⊗t is exactly the relations quotienting B^n. By the finitely-presented injectivity from [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test], the class of x in A⊗_R Q is zero. Exactness of A⊗R^m -> A⊗R^n -> A⊗Q -> 0 therefore gives z_j∈A with h₁(e_i)=∑_j a_{ij}z_j. Define k₁:R^m->A by k₁(d_j)=z_j; then k₁g₁=h₁. Put h₂' = h₂ - i k₁. Then h₂'g₁=0, so h₂' descends uniquely along g₂ to s:C -> B with s g₂=h₂'. Finally p s g₂=p h₂' = p h₂ = g₂, and surjectivity of g₂ gives p s=id_C. This is the (2)->(3)->(4)->(5) argument of Tag 058K with the relation matrix oriented as in its proof, applied to P=C and φ=id_C.

source.place: Tag 058K, theorem-universally-exact-criteria, proof of (2) implies (3), (3) implies (4), and (4) implies (5), applied to P=C and φ=id_C.

proof.text: For each b∈B, the element b-s(p(b)) lies in ker p=i(A), so injectivity of i gives a unique r(b)∈A with i(r(b))=b-s(p(b)). The uniqueness and linearity of this factor through i show that r:B -> A is R-linear. For a∈A, p(i(a))=0, hence i(r(i(a)))=i(a); injectivity of i gives r∘i=id_A. This is exactly the retraction form of the splitting asserted in Tag 058L.
